title: Fibre objects, lifted arrows, finite-type points and versality over the integers
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The integer-base vocabulary consists of $S$, the scheme $T$ regarded over $S$ by its unique structure morphism for each scheme $T$, and each scheme morphism regarded as a morphism over $S$. Let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category over this base (in particular one may take a category fibred in groupoids as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]). For $T\to S$, let $\operatorname{Object}(\mathcal F,T)$ be the fibre of $p$ over $T$, retaining the objects with their specified equality of base and their arrows over $\operatorname{id}_T$. For $a:T\to U$ and fibre objects $z$ over $T$ and $x$ over $U$, let $\operatorname{Lift}(a,z,x)$ be the set of total-category arrows $z\to x$ lying over the specified base map $a$. A point $u\in U$ is of finite type if the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type, meaning locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-residue-field]. For $x\in\operatorname{Object}(\mathcal F,U)$ define $\operatorname{IsVersalAt}(\mathcal F,U,x,u)$ by the following lifting condition (on a fibred groupoid, this is versality). For every pair of commutative Artinian local rings $A,A'$ and surjective residue maps $\rho:A\to\kappa(u)$, $\rho':A'\to\kappa(u)$ whose kernels are their respective maximal ideals, every surjection $g:A'\to A$ with nilpotent kernel and $\rho\circ g=\rho'$, every $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ satisfying $a\circ\operatorname{Spec}\rho=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$, every pair of fibre objects $y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $y'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A'$, and arrows $b:y\to y'$ over $\operatorname{Spec}g$ and $c:y\to x$ over $a$, there exist $a':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an arrow $d:y'\to x$ over $a'$ such that $a'\circ\operatorname{Spec}g=a$ and $d\circ b=c$. Here Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize, local means having a unique maximal ideal, and the displayed residue maps and equation specify the common residue-field identifications. For a fibred groupoid the arrows $b,c,d$ are cartesian, so the last equation requires the lift to extend the specified reduction isomorphism, not only its isomorphism class.
